label: Cua Driver Bench
summary: Each unit is one task of the bench under one of its two conditions: one trial of the bench's own Linux launcher, run whole and unchanged in a container of its XFCE desktop. The launcher resets the task, places its windows, arms its witness window and its guard (in the background condition that window is a simulated user who types in front), then holds its agent's slot open while an agent acts through the computer port, one step for each acting call; at the end it runs the task's own checker and writes the trial's row. The row gives the verdict.

computer.summary: The unit's desktop for an agent: the computer port's pipe (the nullius package's standard/computer_pipe.py, whose path setup gives as the first argument) joined to the socket where this driver serves the port's MCP server, its second argument.

limits.attempts: The bench's run index: attempt k is run index k - 1, from which its launcher draws the trial's seed (the first 8 hex digits of the sha256 of task:index, modulo 10^6), the same for a retried attempt.

datasets.label: Foreground
datasets.summary: The bench's ten core tasks (taskpack/v2-taskset.json) in its foreground condition on its Linux desktop: the agent may take the focus.

datasets.label: Background
datasets.summary: The eight of those tasks the task list gives a background condition: a simulated user's window stays in front and types; a trial passes when the task's check passes, the guard saw no violation and the bench's eight measures show that user undisturbed.

datasets.label: All tasks
datasets.summary: Each task of the list under each of its conditions, its foreground unit then its background unit: 18 units, two pass rules. Its total adds passes of both.

score.says: the bench's own verdict as its launcher writes it in the trial's row. Foreground: passed when the task's checker passed and the guard saw no violation of acting through the screen alone. Background: the bench's background completion, which also needs its eight measures of the simulated user's window measured and held. The checker's partial score, its named checks and the eight measures are in the detail. A check that passes when the agent's time runs out counts, as in the launcher's row

max_steps.label: Steps per task
max_steps.summary: The most acting calls an agent may make on a task: the port's step budget. 45, the bench's limit of 45 turns; the bench counts its own agent's turns, the port counts acting calls.

pause.label: Pause after each action (seconds)
pause.summary: How long the loop waits after each action before the step's picture is taken, to let the screen settle. 1 second, the pause of the port's conformance kit.

desktop_image.label: Desktop image
desktop_image.summary: The image each trial's desktop runs: build, the entry's recipe on the bench's public Linux image, made once on the machine; or the name of an image already on the machine (it is not pulled).

about.build: the bench's public Linux image at a digest, its two provisioning scripts at the pin, and pyautogui and Pillow for the port's actions: about 3.5 GB of downloads the first time

desktop_memory.label: Desktop memory
desktop_memory.summary: The most memory each trial's desktop may use, given to the container engine as its memory limit, in gigabytes or megabytes. A program left running in the desktop then cannot take the machine's memory.

docker.label: Docker for the desktops
docker.summary: Docker on the machine, usable without sudo, or Podman under that name: each trial's desktop is a container of its own, with no network.

nop.from: Nullius: no agent runs; the bench's launcher runs the trial with a command in its agent's slot that does nothing, then the task's own checker reads the untouched desktop.
